subject: Information Theory
title: Amplitude Modulation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Amplitude Modulation.

hook.text: AM radio has broadcast since the 1920s. The signal's strength rises and falls to carry the sound wave's shape.

buildup.text: Amplitude modulation varies the carrier wave's height proportionally to the message signal.

discovery.text: AM is simple and cheap. One detector circuit can demodulate it. That simplicity made radio accessible worldwide.

twist.text: AM is highly vulnerable to noise. Noise directly corrupts amplitude, so AM signals degrade in storms and near machines.

climax.text: FM largely replaced AM for music because frequency is more noise-resistant than amplitude.

punchline.text: Vary the height. Simple but fragile.

quiz.question: Why is AM radio vulnerable to noise?
options: Noise directly affects the signal's amplitude
